We understand what we need to do, and we’re excited to get another chance.” Game 4 is a chance Golden State doesn’t take lightly, a window of opportunity that can and will close in an instant. Either they tie the series up heading back to their raucous home crowd in Ballhalla, or they find themselves in the quicksand of a 3-1 deficit and on the brink of their magic run to the Finals dissipating into dust. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) As such, the Valkyries require making some major adjustments to stifle the Dream, who’ve set the tone the entire series thus far. From Angel Reese steamrolling them to the cup and giving them the “petite” gesture, along the way to Atlanta as a whole squeezing the life out of the Golden State offense and forcing them into uncharacteristic turnovers, it’s adapt or go extinct for the Valkyries at this juncture of the series. So here are three aspects of the series the Valkyries need to address and adjust to even things up at 2-2 and get back to their brand of unrelenting, strength-in-numbers basketball. The Valkyries must uncork the halfcourt offense It’s not surprising that Golden State’s been rendered completely ineffective in the halfcourt this series. After all, the Dream boast the Defensive Player of the Year and have the length and athleticism to blunt a lot of what the Valkyries like to do best, specifically their drive-and-kick, stampede actions – where a player catches the ball on the run as they cut after the initiator draws the defense. Nor has it been a surprise when it seems like every single shot Golden State attempts has a hand in their face or a Dream defender all the way in their airspace– the Valkyries boasted one of the toughest shot difficulties all season long, with their best shotmakers having some of the lower expected field goal percentages in the league. But it has been a decisive factor in the tenor of this series. Atlanta has completely taken away Golden State’s transition opportunities, the part of the game where their offense is cleanest and when the Valkyries can unload the avalanche on teams, making their halfcourt execution even more important. So far this series, they haven’t come close to cracking the Dream’s shell defense, designed to gap their drives and force them into 1-on-1 iso basketball. So the Valkyries know what they need to do: score more points in the halfcourt. Obviously. But how they do that is the real conundrum. Because while Gabby Williams has risen to a star-level talent these playoffs, her on-ball will just never draw two defenders to her in the way a truly A1 offensive talent demands, which is not a knock on her, just a statement of fact for how Atlanta has defended her this series. And while it’s easy to say “scrap the scheme” when the scheme isn’t working, you can’t just do that in the middle of a Finals series; you don’t have time. So at this juncture, Golden State is going to have to lean on their strength-in-numbers philosophy to solve the Dream’s defense. That could mean leaning more into the depth that has done well offensively this series. Tiffany Hayes seems like the one Valkyrie who can consistently punch the paint. Janelle Salaun came alive in Game 3; at her best, she can overcome a hand in her face and bury any-and-all catch-and-shoot triples. From Williams’ point of view, it comes down to being more decisive, which melds into coach Natalie Nakase’s point about cutting down on turnovers. Overall, the Valkyries have been controlling the tempo, reducing possessions, and getting extra possessions from steals and offensive rebounds. Those are key factors that can certainly help loosen up their offensive slog. But the fact of the matter is they’ll just need to make some tough buckets. A simple solution, but hard to make a reality with the way Atlanta’s defending. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images The Valkyries must slow down Angel Reese On the flip side, and a far more controllable variable than their high-variance offense, is the Valkyries’ defense, which still hasn’t solved Reese, despite that side of the court being the defining trait of their run to the Finals. It’s not for a lack of effort. Golden State has used center Kiah Stokes with some success, but it comes at the cost of clogging their offense’s spacing. And when Stokes hasn’t been on the floor, Reese has literally burned everyone else. Aminata Gueye? Torched – and trash-talked along the way. Kayla Thornton? Not big enough and not quick enough. Salaun? Hasn’t been fast enough laterally for the quick Reese. Laeticia Amihere? Outmuscled whenever she doesn’t have a help defender behind her to deter Reese. So what’s the adjustment? Well, it’s not as simple as showing two at Reese or loading up the help behind her like they did to A’ja Wilson in the Las Vegas Aces series. For one, the Dream are doing a great job putting her in spots that make it terrible tactically to do either of those things, unless you are comfortable with any one of her four teammates getting a wide-open shot, something Wilson didn’t really have the luxury of. And for another, it may just be better to let Reese get hers and keep every other Dream player locked up and out of rhythm. The Valkyries’ defense got completely worked when Reese started getting everyone else involved. Whether it was her leading the break or finding the right pass when all eyes were on her, she’s deadliest when she’s bullying the Valkyries enough to send even more resources at her. That doesn’t mean don’t guard her. Nakase should probably be matching Stokes minutes with her at this point – and find a way to make her more useful offensively – and Amihere has a case for getting more run against her. Maybe even throw Kaila Charles at her. She’s had the most fight and energy of any Valkyrie these Finals, as she didn’t back down when she and Rhyne Howard got into it. It also helps that she played with Reese in AAU on Team Takeover in Maryland; she might intuitively remember some age-old secrets to defending her. But ultimately, Golden State needs to limit her on the offensive boards; she has 11 in the Finals and had five in Game 3. Again, easier said than done against the best rebounder in the league. But those kinds of plays become back-breaking over the course of a game, and if they want to win the possession battle, it behooves the Valkyries to consider boxing her out with even more attention. Kelley L Cox-Imagn Images The Valkyries must find the fire and get back to Golden State basketball But X’s and O’s and tactics aside, the Valkyries believe their shortcomings in Games 2 and 3 all stem from not playing like themselves. And wrapped into that is the way Reese and the Dream have won the mind game battle in how she’s fired herself up with the trash talk. Those kinds of things give Atlanta their edge – their motivation. The Valkyries have motivation; it just hasn’t translated into their hoops. And they know it . “We need to have some fire, too,” Charles said when asked about how Reese has gone at Gueye specifically and how the Valkyries as a whole deal with those kinds of interactions. “People (don’t) necessarily (have to be) trash talkers, but being more physical, imposing our will, and dictating the game that way.” Charles’ answer

item.title: ‘Would They Admit This if Bucs Lost?’ ‘Enough Is Enough’ — NFL Fans React As League Admits ‘Embarrassing Officiating Mistake’ in Cowboys’ Loss
item.description: ‘Would They Admit This if Bucs Lost?’ ‘Enough Is Enough’ — NFL Fans React As League Admits 'Embarrassing Officiating Mistake' in Cowboys’ Loss Tampa Bay Buccaneers defensive tackle Calijah Kancey was flagged for illegal hands to the face in the Bucs’ 24-16 win over the Dallas Cowboys on October 8. The NFL has now acknowledged that Kancey did not commit the foul and that the only relevant hand contact on the play came from Cowboys guard Tyler Booker. The result has long since been entered into the books. It’s been more than two weeks since the game, but fans were far from willing to let this one slide. NFL Acknowledges Referees Penalized the Wrong Team in Cowboys-Bucs In the video, NFL officiating and rules analyst Walt Anderson walked through the Week 5 play by jersey number. Kancey wears No. 94 for Tampa Bay, and Booker wears No. 52 for Dallas. Anderson said, “We’re going to have a foul called on No. 94 on the defensive team for illegal hands to the face … The only action relative to any hands is really by the offensive player here … Because it’s clearly not a foul by No. 94. If there is illegal use of hands, it’s obviously by No. 52 of the offense.” Pro Football Talk’s Michael David Smith called the wrong-team flag “a rather embarrassing officiating mistake.” SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer Smith reported that the call was miscommunicated as Kancey’s foul, which is how the yardage was stepped off against the Bucs. He also wrote that Kancey “made clear in the moment that he knew it was a bad call.” Fox Sports reporter Greg Auman wrote on Friday night, “As many of you pointed out in real time, an admission from officials that the wrong team was flagged Sunday.” One fan suggested a blanket solution: “Everything should be reviewable. Enough is enough.” So why didn’t anyone fix it on the spot? Anderson’s explanation points to a safeguard meant for this kind of mix-up. “This is the type of play that the Competition Committee has instructed officiating that if objective information in terms of just asking the officials, ‘Are we sure we have the right number of the player here?’ that we can end up assisting with this.” Smith also wrote in his column that “The New York officiating office could have fixed it, but didn’t.” Another fan came to the same conclusion : “I mean there’s video evidence. item.title: Raptors’ Darko Rajakovic gives props to Toronto for tough team win over Wizards
item.description: Nick Turchiaro-Imagn Images Raptors’ Darko Rajakovic gives props to Toronto for tough team win over Wizards appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Darko Rajaković has Toronto Raptors fans believing this team can win in more ways than one. That’s after guiding his squad to a gritty 112-102 road victory over the Washington Wizards on Friday. Following their 43-point blowout on opening night, the Raptors faced a tougher challenge at Capital One Arena. However, they held firm down the stretch to improve to 2-0 in the 2026-27 NBA season. Rajaković praised his team’s resilience after the game. He emphasized the importance of finding ways to win when shots are not falling consistently. "The fight in finding a way to win tonight was very important." Darko Rajaković speaks to the media following the Raptors' 112-102 win over the Wizards. pic.twitter.com/1iJxGCZhrX Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — Sportsnet (@Sportsnet) October 24, 2026 “The fight in finding a way to win tonight was very important,” he told reporters. Toronto backed up that mentality with a commanding performance inside. The Raptors outrebounded Washington 53-40, grabbed 19 offensive boards, and outscored the Wizards 52-32 in the paint. Scottie Barnes led the way with 28 points, 14 rebounds, and five assists. RJ Barrett contributed 23 points and nine rebounds. Kawhi Leonard added 16 points, nine boards, and three steals in 28 minutes. Toronto also received a major lift from its bench. Collin Murray-Boyles finished plus-21, and Ja’Kobe Walter posted a plus-19. The victory showcased Rajaković’s ability to adapt his approach and keep his team composed when the game turned into a physical grind. Rajaković enters his fourth season as Toronto’s head coach with a fresh multi-year extension and renewed expectations. His high-movement offensive system produced a 43-point opening-night rout of Chicago. Friday’s performance, though, showed the Raptors can also prevail through rebounding, defense, and second-chance opportunities. Rajaković has Toronto off to an encouraging start. They now face another early test against Anthony Edwards and the Minnesota Timberwolves on Sunday. item.title: Norris faster than Verstappen and Leclerc in Austin long-run comparison
item.description: Max Verstappen had to settle for second place behind Charles Leclerc in both practice sessions in Austin, but the gap has almost disappeared in the long runs. The two posted virtually identical averages on the soft tyres. That offers Red Bull Racing hope for Sunday, although Mercedes and McLaren 's tyre choices leave the door open for their rivals. Leclerc ended both sessions at the Circuit of The Americas as the fastest driver . Verstappen was 0.084 seconds off the pace in the first practice session, while the gap grew to 0.189 seconds in FP2. Kimi Antonelli managed to slot in between the Ferrari and the Red Bull. Over a single lap, then, Leclerc had the edge on Friday. Verstappen was not entirely satisfied with his car at the start of the weekend. Red Bull began on the hard tyres, before the Dutchman switched to softs. On that compound, he was already close to Leclerc, despite his earlier complaints about the car's handling. The first laps on the mediums followed in FP2, and Verstappen seemed to find a better balance. Verstappen and Leclerc almost inseparable The comparison becomes more interesting for Red Bull once the drivers embark on their longer runs. Verstappen posted an average of 1:41.481 over eleven laps on the softs. Leclerc averaged 1:41.479 over the first eleven laps of his long run on the same compound. Based on the rounded times, the difference is just two thousandths of a second. That means the gap seen in the qualifying simulations has almost completely disappeared over this stint. The runs do differ a little in how they unfold, however. Leclerc posts three consecutive laps under 1:41 early in his stint, while Verstappen dips below that mark just once. Later on, the Ferrari driver more often goes above 1:42. After his slowest lap, a 1:42.188, Verstappen gets back down to 1:41.555 and 1:41.401. That is encouraging for Red Bull. Verstappen also maintains a fairly consistent pace further into the stint. Leclerc starts faster, but does not sustain that advantage over these eleven laps. Fuel loads and the tyres' earlier usage are unknown, so no definitive conclusions about tyre wear can be drawn from this data yet. Mercedes and McLaren run different tyres The virtually identical averages do not mean, however, that the race will automatically be a contest between Verstappen and Leclerc. Antonelli averages 1:41.521 on the mediums, putting him just four hundredths behind Verstappen. However, three outliers have been excluded from the Italian's average. As a result, his figure is less directly comparable with the Red Bull driver's complete set of laps. Norris also deserves attention. The McLaren driver averages 1:41.289 on the hard tyres across the selected laps. That makes him faster than both Verstappen and Leclerc on softs. One slower lap has also been excluded for Norris, and his stint is shorter, but his pace gives Red Bull ample reason to keep an eye on McLaren. item.description: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images Mavericks HC Dusty May gives initial Cooper Flagg injury diagnosis after hard fall on shoulder vs. Pacers appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Dallas Mavericks came away from Indiana with a blowout win, but they may also be bracing for some uncertainty surrounding Cooper Flagg . Flagg exited Friday night’s 121-105 victory over the Indiana Pacers at Gainbridge Fieldhouse with a left shoulder injury and did not return. After the game, head coach Dusty May gave an initial update , saying Flagg was dealing with left shoulder soreness and “will be evaluated” in the next couple of days. The injury came with under a minute left in the first half. Flagg appeared to be headed for a breakaway dunk when Pacers swingman Aaron Nesmith fouled him hard from behind. The contact knocked Flagg off balance, and he landed awkwardly on his shoulder under the basket. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Flagg was checked by a trainer after the play. He kept rubbing his shoulder as he walked to the locker room and did not come out for the second half. The play quickly boiled over. Naji Marshall confronted Nesmith after the foul, and players from both teams got involved in a brief shoving match along the baseline before coaches and officials separated them. Nesmith was assessed a Flagrant 1, and a double technical was handed to Nesmith and Marshall. Before leaving, Flagg was having a terrific night. The second-year forward had 14 points, six assists, five rebounds and three steals in just 17 minutes, helping Dallas build a commanding 77-43 halftime lead. The Mavericks cruised from there without him. Dallas will be hoping for good news on the evaluation, especially with a tough test right around the corner. The Mavericks host Victor Wembanyama and the San Antonio Spurs on Saturday night at American Airlines Center, then visit the Miami Heat on Monday. With the evaluation coming over the next couple of days, there was no immediate word on Flagg’s status for the matchup with the Spurs. Flagg, the No. 1 overall pick in the 2025 NBA Draft out of Duke, is the centerpiece of Dallas’ future and a key part of May’s plans in his first season leading the team . Any extended absence would be a significant blow for a Mavericks squad that looked sharp in Indiana. For now, the Mavericks will wait on the results and hope the soreness is nothing more than that. item.title: “Bye Bye Stephanie White” – WNBA Fans Erupt As Caitlin Clark Likes Fever’s Kelly Krauskopf Exit Post
item.description: Indiana Fever guard Caitlin Clark speaks with media members Thursday, Oct. 8, 2026, at Gainbridge Fieldhouse in Indianapolis. The Indiana Fever have failed to get past the Las Vegas Aces for the second straight year. Just three weeks after Caitlin Clark and her teammates were eliminated in the first round, the Fever announced that team president Kelly Krauskopf would be stepping down. The team then posted a quote from team owner Herb Simon commenting on Krauskopf’s exit. Eagle-eyed fans quickly noticed that Clark had apparently “liked” the post on Instagram. Sure enough, the reactions poured in, with some fans speculating that Fever coach Stephanie White might also be shown the door. “Haha @caitlinclark22 approves bye bye Stephanie White,” one fan tweeted . Krauskopf, who played college basketball at Texas A&M, was the Fever’s first-ever president and general manager when the team entered the WNBA in 2000. Over the next 18 years, the team went on a 12-year playoff streak, culminating in 2012 when a Tamika Catchings-led squad won the WNBA title. After six years as the Indiana Pacers’ assistant general manager, Krauskopf returned to the Fever in 2024 as president of basketball and business operations. Though Krauskopf has a proven track record, she reportedly told the Fever about her decision to step down before the season ended . Report: Fever Fire Amber Cox, Set to Search for GM “To Build Around Aliyah Boston and Caitlin Clark” Krauskopf wasn’t the only Fever executive to make headlines on Friday. Hours after the Krauskopf news broke, IndyStar reported that the team was firing GM Amber Cox. “Indiana Fever will search for a GM to build around Aliyah Boston and Caitlin Clark, facing big decisions this offseason,” IndyStar tweeted . During Cox’s first season with the Fever, her mettle as GM was tested as the team dealt with multiple season-ending injuries to players like Caitlin Clark and Sophie Cunningham. To Cox’s credit, the players that she signed to hardship contracts (such as Aari McDonald and Odyssey Sims) helped the team stay afloat and even advance to the second round of the 2025 playoffs. This season, however, Cox’s roster construction has come under even more scrutiny as a high-octane Fever squad ultimately fell short against the Aces in the first round. Now, her successor will have to decide whether to extend Clark’s contract and re-sign Mitchell. item.title: MSU hockey shut out on the road for first loss at New Hampshire
item.description: The No. 2 Michigan State hockey team dropped its first contest of the season on Oct. 23, falling 1-0 on the road against New Hampshire in the first if a two-game series with the Wildcats. Both sides skated to a 0-0 tie through two periods before New Hampshire broke through with a power play goal from Emile Guite with 11 minutes remaining in the third period. "We didn’t do enough to win a hockey game tonight, and to me, there’s a difference between being expected to win and being entitled to win, and we’re definitely not entitled to win any hockey games," MSU coach Adam Nightingale said. "We’ve got to go out and earn it, and I refuse to say to our guys that we're just young, because when you start to go down that path you give the guys an excuse. Our guys are good enough and smart enough, and (New Hampshire) is a good team and we'll have to be better if we want to have success tomorrow." The Spartans were outshot 34-14 and had 12 shots blocked by Wildcat defenders in the contest. Freshman goaltender Joshua Ravensbergen made 33 saves to set a new career high, and MSU was unable to convert on its lone chance with the man advantage. MSU (3-1-0) will face New Hampshire again on Oct. 24 with puck drop scheduled for 7 p.m. The game will be streamed on ESPN+. item.description: Nobody can protect the ball against Dyson Daniels right now originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Atlanta Hawks guard Dyson Daniels is wasting no time reminding the NBA why he is considered one of the league's most disruptive perimeter defenders. Through the first two games of the season, Daniels has already recorded an impressive 12 steals, demonstrating the defensive instincts, quick hands, and relentless effort that have made him a nightmare for opposing ball handlers. While scoring performances typically dominate headlines around the NBA, Daniels is proving that defense can be just as impactful. His ability to anticipate passing lanes, pressure opposing guards, and create turnovers has provided Atlanta with an important defensive presence early in the season. For the Hawks, Daniels' production represents more than an impressive individual statistic. His defensive activity creates additional transition opportunities, allowing Atlanta to push the basketball and generate easier scoring chances. Daniels recorded five steals in Atlanta's 132-125 season-opening victory over the Orlando Magic , finishing with 20 points, four rebounds, and three assists. Daniels making case for defensive player of the year He followed that performance with seven steals in Friday's dominant 128-81 victory over the Charlotte Hornets . Daniels also contributed 11 points, nine rebounds, and four assists as Atlanta improved to 2-0. His 12 steals are the most by any NBA player through the first two games of a season this century. Following Friday's victory, Daniels acknowledged that Charlotte made some costly mistakes. "In this game they were just giving it to me, I'm not going to lie. They were throwing it in my hands," Daniels said. The Australian guard's defensive performance is quickly becoming one of the biggest storylines surrounding Atlanta's undefeated start. With Daniels leading the defensive charge, the Hawks are showing early signs of becoming a dangerous team in the Eastern Conference. If Daniels maintains anything close to this production, another All-Defensive selection could be within reach. For now, one thing is clear: opposing teams must be extremely careful whenever Daniels is guarding the basketball. (Photo by Aaron Gash/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images The Tampa Bay Rays had a World Series Game 1 win on the line multiple times. They just could not reel it in. Tampa Bay dropped Game 1 of the World Series 3-2 to the Milwaukee Brewers on Friday night. A ninth-inning rally, kept alive by a replay review, ended with the tying run on third base when Jonny DeLuca struck out against Trevor Megill. Between a ball that popped out of a glove and two double plays that caught two runners stealing, the Rays had their hands on this one several times. The Brewers lead the series 1-0, and if the rest of the series is anything like this one, everybody is in for a ride. The first near miss came three batters in. Jonathan Aranda and Chandler Simpson singled, but Junior Caminero lined a ball right at third baseman David Hamilton, who doubled Aranda off second. The bottom half was where the first opportunity slipped free. After Jackson Chourio led off with a single against Nick Martinez, Christian Yelich drove one to deep center, where it bounced out of DeLuca’s glove. Instead of a long out, it was an RBI triple. William Contreras followed with a single that caromed off shortstop Taylor Walls into left, and Milwaukee led 2-0 before the Rays could settle in. What a way to start the World Series! item.description: Erik Spoelstra is not worried about the Heat's struggles to start the 2026-27 season originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After the 2026 offseason, the Miami Heat had immense hype surrounding the team. With Giannis Antetokounmpo, anything is possible, but people are down on the Heat right now because of their slow start to the 2026-27 season. They have lost their first two games of the season to the Minnesota Timberwolves and the Detroit Pistons . Both are formidable opponents, but the second loss in a row does not have head coach Erik Spoelstra worried just yet. Erik Spoelstra is unbothered by the two losses to start the Heat's season It has not been the best stretch for the Heat to start the season because a lot of people expected them to at least win one game from the first two. Unfortunately, they were trounced by both opponents. Now, Spoelstra is back to the drawing board after a nightmare start to the year. As the head coach, he wants to stabilize the team amid all the struggles they are currently facing. MORE: Erik Spoelstra wants to build a healthy dynamic with Giannis Antetokounmpo Of course, it is only two games into an 82-game season, so it is not the time to panic. Spoelstra has those sentiments, but he is looking for the best ways to resolve the problems they had during the first two games. "We're facing a little bit of adversity to start. No one wanted to start 0-2 with our first two home games. I do know this about our locker room: they care... Giannis really cares. He wants this to work; his teammates really want this to work. We're gonna get there," Spoelstra said after the loss to the Pistons . As long as the players can channel their frustrations into bouncing back, the Heat will be okay. However, they would have preferred to have a win on the board, but at the moment, they will have to motivate themselves. item.title: Shedeur Sanders faces Browns demotion threat as Dillon Gabriel gets second-team reps
item.description: Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images Shedeur Sanders could be pushed further down the Cleveland Browns’ quarterback depth chart after Dillon Gabriel began taking second-team offensive reps in practice. Sanders has served as Deshaun Watson’s backup this season, but Gabriel’s increased involvement raises questions about his place in Cleveland’s plans once the injured rookie returns. item.title: “LeBron James Hates the Country that Made Him a Billionaire”: Journalist Sounds Off After Golf Swing Practice During National Anthem
item.description: LeBron James © X/ @Sixers LeBron James has started his 76ers career with a bang. Philadelphia beat the defending-champion Knicks, 106-100, in his first game. In his second game, the 76ers beat James’ former team, the Cavaliers, 114-106 on Thursday. He had 14 points, nine rebounds, and seven assists in the first game, and 17 points, 10 rebounds, five assists, and three steals in the second. However, his strong start is the least-discussed part of James’ season. James has faced backlash after he was seen practicing his golf swing during the national anthem on Tuesday. Among others, journalist Clay Travis also presented his negative views on James’ actions. “LeBron would never disrespect the Chinese national anthem like he did the American national anthem this week. LeBron hates the country that made him a billionaire. His brain is broken,” Travis captioned his post. “This is insanely disrespectful. The President was right to call him out for this. He knows all the cameras are gonna be on him. It’s not only disrespectful to everyone that has given him this tremendous opportunity but the singer is on the floor right there, singing the national anthem. A highly trained, Grammy winning, Broadway celebrity, who is there putting their heart and soul in that performance. Everyone else on the entire team is able to behave like an adult,” Travis said . President Donald Trump calls out LeBron James President Trump was fuming after LeBron’s actions during the national anthem. “While listening to our National Anthem, LeBron James disrespects our Country! I said right from the beginning that he’s no good, a TOTAL DISGRACE. LeBron James should apologize to all of those Great American Warriors and Heroes who died for the American Flag, and all that our Country stands for! President DONALD J. TRUMP,” he said on Truth Social. LeBron brushed off the controversy, calling it a “slow news day,” to the reporter who asked for his reply to Trump’s comments. item.title: Tiago Splitter explains approach to adjusting starting lineups after Bucks win
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Brad Repplinger-Imagn Images Tiago Splitter explains approach to adjusting starting lineups after Bucks win appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Chicago Bulls bounced back from a 43-point loss to the Toronto Raptors by defeating the Milwaukee Bucks 132-125. They also made a 15-point comeback. It was a case of: it wasn’t about how you start, but how you finish. The starting lineup consisted of Caleb Wilson, Norman Powell, Matas Buzelis, Josh Giddey, and Jalen Smith. In the end, Giddey, Smith, and Buzelis sat on the bench. Instead, Leonard Miller, Tre Jones, and Isaac Okoro played with Wilson and Powell to cap off the game. After the game, head coach Tiago Splitter explained his decision to use different lineups based on the circumstances, per Will Gottlieb of CHGO_Bulls. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “You’ve got to see, game-by-game, who’s going to finish the game. But you cannot change the starting lineup every time a guy plays well or plays bad. If not, you go crazy; you change every game.” Tiago on his approach to the starting and closing lineups: "You've got to see, game-by-game, who's going to finish the game. But you cannot change the starting lineup every time a guy plays well or plays bad. If not, you go crazy, you change every game." pic.twitter.com/xgg5vQjIK0 — Will Gottlieb (@WillGottlieb) October 23, 2026 In the end, the changing of the lineups worked out for everyone. Plus, they got the best out of many of those players. Powell finished the game as the leading scorer with 25 points and went 9-for-9 at the free-throw line. Additionally, Caleb Wilson finished with 21 points and 6 rebounds. Miller came off the bench to add 19 points. Okoro scored 12 points, and Jones added 11 points. Also, Buddy Hield added 13 points. However, Giddey and Buzelis finished with low numbers. Buzelis scored 7 points, and Giddey scored 6. Giddey was listed as probable on the injured list before the game with a left wrist injury. The Bulls will play the Washington Wizards in their home opener on Saturday. Related: Caleb Wilson makes a bold declaration after first NBA win with Bulls Related: Is Josh Giddey playing? item.description: Photo by: Matt Marton Yelich Gives Milwaukee an Early Spark The Brewers wasted little time getting on the scoreboard. Christian Yelich delivered an RBI triple in the bottom of the first inning to give Milwaukee a 1-0 lead. William Contreras followed with an RBI single, extending the advantage to 2-0 and immediately putting pressure on Tampa Bay’s pitching staff. On the mound, rookie right-hander Jacob Misiorowski made an impression early. He fired a 103.5 mph pitch, setting a World Series velocity record in the pitch-tracking era. His electric fastball gave Milwaukee a major weapon as the Brewers attempted to keep Tampa Bay’s lineup under control. The Rays finally broke through in the fourth inning when Liam Hicks grounded out to bring home a run, cutting the deficit to 2-1. Tampa Bay continued looking for opportunities, but Milwaukee’s pitching and defense limited the damage. Chourio Adds an Important Insurance Run Milwaukee regained a two run cushion in the seventh inning. Jackson Chourio delivered an RBI single to make it 3-1, giving the Brewers a valuable insurance run heading into the final innings. The hit proved crucial as Tampa Bay continued battling. The Rays threatened in the ninth, cutting the deficit to one run when Liam Hicks brought home a runner. Tampa Bay also attempted a double steal to put the tying run in scoring position, creating a tense situation for Milwaukee’s bullpen. item.title: Arman Tsarukyan steps on Dillon Danis after shutout victory in RAF 14 main event
item.description: Arman Tsarukyan nearly set off another chaotic scene when he stepped on Dillon Danis following a dominant win in the RAF 14 main event. One day removed from Tsarukyan actually attacking Danis at the pre-event press conference, security was on high alert come Friday night. In the actual match, Tsarukyan barely broke a sweat as he scored takedowns and turns to quickly rack up 10 points to end the match by tech fall. But as soon as the match ended, Tsarukyan actually stepped on Danis as he was getting back to his feet and it appeared a melee was inevitable. But this time the RAF staff was prepared as security flooded the mats to keep the athletes separated. Despite the contentious ending, Danis actually stood and shook Tsarukyan’s hand afterwards, although the top ranked UFC lightweight contender doesn’t consider the rivalry settled. “No it’s over if we fight together,” Tsarukyan said. “I’m wrestling back to back with high level grapples. Come to support me in Abu Dhabi.” Tsarukyan seemingly slapped Danis to open the match before scoring with a push out as the referee issued a quick warning. Tsarukyan then snatched a takdedown for another two points before restart on the feet. Another step out point for Tsarukyan put him up four before he snatched a takedown and that led to another quick series of points getting racked up. Before he knew it, Tsarkyan was up 10-0 to end the match by technical superiority in the first period. When the match ended, Tsarukyan stepped on Danis as he got up off the mat as security flooded the mats before mayhem could unfold. To his credit, Danis kept his cool and didn’t retaliate as security kept them apart. Now Tsarukyan prepares for his next match in three weeks in Abu Dhabi while holding out hope that his next fight comes against UFC lightweight champion Justin Gaethje.

item.title: Jayson Tatum Takes Over Late as Celtics Defeat Knicks
item.description: Photo by: Rick Osentoski The Boston Celtics earned an impressive 107-103 victory over the New York Knicks on Friday night, using a dominant third quarter and a clutch performance from Jayson Tatum to secure their first home win of the 2026-27 NBA season. Tatum delivered one of his strongest performances of the young season, finishing with 36 points, nine rebounds and seven assists. After a relatively quiet first half, the Celtics star took control after halftime, scoring 25 of his points in the second half and delivering several crucial baskets down the stretch. Paul George and Neemias Queta also contributed 15 points apiece, helping Boston withstand a late push from the defending NBA champion Knicks. Celtics Build Momentum in the Third Quarter The opening half featured plenty of back-and-forth action, with neither team able to create much separation. New York held a narrow 49-50 deficit at halftime after a competitive first two quarters that included multiple lead changes. Boston found another gear coming out of the locker room. The Celtics outscored the Knicks 33-24 in the third quarter, creating breathing room heading into the final period. Tatum led the charge, attacking the basket and finding opportunities to score from the perimeter. Boston’s offense became more efficient, while its defense made it difficult for New York to maintain consistency. The Celtics eventually built their advantage to 91-79, putting themselves in position to close out the game. Tatum Delivers When It Matters Most New York refused to go away quietly. The Knicks put together a 12-3 run to cut Boston’s lead to 94-91, setting up a tense finish at TD Garden. After the Knicks continued to threaten, Tatum answered with a difficult jumper to restore some separation. He followed that with another important basket before knocking down a three-pointer late in the fourth quarter. Those shots proved critical as Boston held off the Knicks’ comeback attempt and secured the four-point victory. Karl-Anthony Towns led New York with 22 points and 10 rebounds, while OG Anunoby recorded 20 points, 10 rebounds and eight assists. Deuce McBride also scored 20 points off the bench, and Jalen Brunson finished with 19. Boston Looks to Build on the Win The victory improved Boston’s record to 1-1, giving the Celtics an important early-season boost against a conference rival. Tatum’s late-game execution was the biggest takeaway, particularly with the Knicks threatening to steal the game in the final minutes. Boston will look to carry that momentum into its next matchup against the Chicago Bulls on Monday night.

item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. item.title: Is el clásico still the world’s biggest match? Three questions before Barcelona v Real Madrid
item.description: The fixture’s relevance waned as the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded. Can Lamine Yamal and Mbappé lift it into a new era? For the best part of a decade, el clásico was more than just soccer’s biggest fixture. It was the defining narrative. At the peak of the Lionel Messi v Cristiano Ronaldo era, there were clásicos everywhere. Yes, when the two historic rivals clashed on the pitch, but also in the voting for the Ballon d’Or every year and in so much of the discourse around the sport. As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. In 2026, however, it’s difficult to measure a clásico ’s standing. Is it still the sport’s biggest fixture? Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. item.title: Bournemouth enjoy night to remember as 10-man Milan fail to weather storm
item.description: This was a momentous night in Bournemouth’s history, although the truth is they would have been given a far sterner examination by Coventry or Hull. Whatever this rotten impersonation of a Milan side was, it bore no relation to those that forged such a celebrated history. The visitors resembled holograms even before their goalkeeper Mike Maignan, with an extraordinary rush of blood resulting in a penalty and red card, rendered their task impossible. They never showed the slightest hint of putting up a fight. Bournemouth simply swamped the seven-time European champions and, amid a swirling south coast storm that rarely let up, could depart singing in the rain. Amine Adli’s sumptuous late free-kick, curled left-footed from 22 yards, meant they could finish the evening with the flourish they deserved. Their joy was clear at full time and met disapproval from some of Milan’s staff, who appeared to take umbrage in a short-lived fracas near the tunnel afterwards. Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
